title: Auto-Continuation on Output Token Limit
description: Claude Code v2.1.90 introduces automatic continuation when a response is truncated by the output token limit. Previously, a cut-off response required the user to manually prompt 'continue' or retry. Now Claude Code detects the truncation and continues automatically. Directly pipeline-relevant: evaluation files, registry updates, and discovery summaries generated by claude -p automation occasionally exceed output limits and produce partial files requiring human retry logic. If auto-continuation applies to -p (non-interactive) mode, this is a zero-config reliability improvement for the heartbeat and iterative-improve pipelines.
redundancy_notes: No existing auto-continuation mechanism in registry. Existing workaround: manual 'continue' prompts and retry logic in scripts. Classification: NOVEL.
unknowns: Does auto-continuation apply to claude -p (non-interactive) mode?
Is there a limit on how many continuations occur automatically?
Does auto-continuation fire another PostToolUse hook cycle?

evaluation.reasoning: Zero integration cost — built-in behavior change, no configuration needed. High pipeline relevance: directly addresses the partial-file / truncated-output failure mode in claude -p automation runs (heartbeat, version investigations, evaluation file generation). Score slightly moderated from maximum (75 vs 80 for capability) due to unconfirmed -p mode applicability — if interactive-only the benefit is meaningful but not pipeline-critical. Even interactive-only, this removes a common manual intervention point. Token efficiency 70: eliminates retry overhead and partial-file cleanup cycles. Official Anthropic v2.1.90 feature, zero maintenance. Integration action: verify -p mode behavior and document in registry. If confirmed for -p: update heartbeat notes to remove manual continuation workarounds.
